chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Sinan, from al-Awn ibn Ma'yan (the hat-seller), from Ibn Abi Ya'foor, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever meets the believers with one face (countenance), but gossips about them in their absence with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection having two tongues of fire.

key_terms.وَجْهٍ: face/countenance (here implying a different manner or speech)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for being two-faced and backbiting believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to illustrate the spiritual danger of *al-wajhan* (having two faces), where outward friendliness masks inner malice. The metaphor of 'two tongues of fire' signifies that the hypocrisy manifested in speech will become a physical reality in the Hereafter, serving as a severe warning against the social sin of backbiting among the faithful. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings, emphasizing that consistency between one's public demeanor and private words is essential for spiritual integrity.
